llm.summary: Three things broke overnight and they all point the same way. First, the macro: Q3 GDP printed +3.4%, the strongest in a year, while September core PCE accelerated — the Fed held but two officials dissented for a HIKE and December hike odds are now above 80%, with the 10-year breaching 5%. Second, the AI capex narrative took its first real crack: Alphabet missed and is down ~10-11% in what would be a record post-earnings loss, with CNBC framing it as the first sign AI is eating search monetization, and critically BOTH Google and Microsoft declined to raise capex forecasts. Microsoft's cloud growth and cash flow were the one offset. Third, software and cyber are de-rating violently and independently of the index — ServiceNow -18.7% premarket, Cognizant cratering on Q4 guidance, Fortinet dragging the whole security complex after F5 did the same, and 24/7 explicitly noting Wall Street has stopped paying security stocks for beats. Caterpillar is headed for its worst day in seven years, confirming Industrials at -45 on flows. Against this, the real-asset side keeps working: Shell nearly doubled profit with European majors lifting buybacks, GE Vernova bought $9B of grid, Quanta and Duke raised, ERCOT flagged a demand surge, and Energy flows sit at 88. Gold is sliding toward $4,000 because the hike is the problem, not the hedge. The regime model now has Stagflation 32.6 (+13.5) and Reflation 31.3 (+12.2) rising together while Goldilocks collapses -13.2 — hot growth, hot prices, higher discount rate. Own cash flow, electrons and pricing power; the discount-rate-dependent trade is being repriced in real time.

market_thesis.short_term: Multiple compression, not an earnings recession. Growth at 3.4% with accelerating PCE removes the Fed put entirely and makes December live; 5% on the 10-year is the mechanism that transmits that into long-duration equities. The specific damage today is concentrated: Comm Services (-82 flows) with Alphabet's record drop, software (ServiceNow, Cognizant), cyber (Fortinet, F5), and Industrials (Caterpillar). Amazon and Intel tonight are the next binary — Amazon's AWS number and capex language will either confirm or refute the 'hyperscalers are pausing capex escalation' read from Google/Microsoft. Expect continued Value>Growth (+52), Energy/Utilities/Health Care leadership, and no bid for small caps.
market_thesis.medium_term: Stagflation-lite into H1 2027 with an inflationary AI buildout layered on top. Consumer spending is flattening after the inflation surge while GDP is being carried by AI investment — that is a narrow, capex-dependent expansion vulnerable to exactly the funding conditions that 5% yields create. The AI trade bifurcates hard: contracted power, grid, gas, nuclear and the physical supply chain (GE Vernova, Quanta, pipelines, Howmet) keep compounding; AI-adjacent software with unproven agent monetisation and seat-based pricing de-rates toward the Cognizant/ServiceNow outcome. Alphabet's miss is the template risk for every incumbent whose revenue depends on a query, a seat or an ad impression that an agent can bypass. Credit and antitrust are the new overhangs on Nvidia specifically (DOJ probe of the $12.9B Hugging Face deal, SpaceX's $40B GPU lease structure, Nscale's $30B IPO) — the buildout is increasingly financed by leases, private credit and equity issuance, all reflexive to rates.
market_thesis.long_term: Electricity and compute remain the durable supercycle: ERCOT demand surging into the 2030s, pipeline owners racing to add capacity, GE Vernova consolidating grid, nuclear units having lives extended in Korea and shuttered German sites evaluated for data centres, shipping looking at reactors. That is a decade of grid, gas, nuclear, copper and semicap spend with policy backing and regulated or contracted returns — the opposite risk profile to the software layer. Structurally, housing undersupply plus a frozen affordability regime (DR Horton guiding down, BoC hiking, mortgage rates sticky) delays household formation and permanently redirects a cohort's spend toward experiences, value retail and health. Health care takes rising share as populations age — metabolic health, continuous monitoring, devices. And geopolitics is now a permanent cost line: EU-China trade retaliation threats, the Huang espionage story, Iran-driven oil profits — supply chains will keep paying a security premium.

short_term: Consumers are trading down, not stopping: spending flattened after the inflation surge while Costco and Walmart hold share and iPhone sales slide on thinner festive discounts — money is moving from aspirational goods to bulk value and necessities.

Retail investors are disengaging from trading: Robinhood reports habits changing dramatically as stock trading cools, while attention shifts to credit products (Gold/Platinum card queries) — a shift from speculation to yield and spend.

Institutional investors are abandoning the correlated mega-cap bloc: BofA clients dumping Meta and Google at a record pace while Energy, Utilities, Health Care and Staples flows accelerate — people want cash flow now, not duration.

Households are feeling electricity as a budget line, not an abstraction: rising searches for electricity bill payment, assistance and calculators — the data-centre power story is becoming a consumer-politics story.
Borrowers are capitulating on housing: DR Horton's weak FY2027 guide, BoC's hike and 5% Treasuries mean buyers are deferring, renting longer, and builders are absorbing the adjustment through margin.
Convenience spend is consolidating rather than growing: DoorDash buying Instacart for $17B is an admission that delivery demand is mature and the game is now cost and basket, not acquisition.
long_term: Energy security becomes a consumer-visible need — bills, reliability, blackout risk — which politically legitimises enormous grid, gas and nuclear capex and makes utilities a growth category rather than a bond proxy.

Knowledge and productivity get unbundled from software seats: if agents answer queries and complete workflows, the unit of value shifts from the licence and the ad impression to the compute and the outcome, permanently compressing a layer of incumbent economics.

Shelter scarcity rewires life sequencing: delayed formation, longer renting, more storage and multi-generational households — supporting storage REITs, value retail and experience spend over durable-goods upgrade cycles.

Health shifts from episodic treatment to continuous management — glucose monitoring, metabolic drugs, device-mediated longevity — as the main discretionary growth category of an ageing, wealthier-at-the-top population.

Status migrates from objects to experiences and optionality: travel search strength, cruise and hotel beat-and-raise, alongside 'fancy cars hold no appeal' retiree psychology — time and freedom outrank possessions.

Sovereignty becomes a product feature across compute, energy and payments — sovereign AI clouds, domestic LNG, Russia's Starlink alternative — fragmenting global markets into regional stacks with duplicated capex.

The decisive new fact: both Google and Microsoft declined to raise capex forecasts. Yesterday the question was how high AI capex would go; today the question is whether it has plateaued.

Microsoft separated from the pack — cloud growth and cash flow lifted the stock while Alphabet collapsed. The Magnificent Seven correlation break that CNBC flagged yesterday is now visible in a single session.

The software and cyber de-rating broadened materially: ServiceNow -18.7%, Cognizant cratering on Q4 guidance, Fortinet dragging security after F5. Markets have stopped paying for beats in these groups.
Caterpillar is headed for its worst day in seven years, converting the Industrials flow reading (-45) into a visible index-level event.
Gold broke lower toward $4,000 — yesterday it was defending $4,040; the December hike has overwhelmed the stagflation hedge bid.

New M&A and regulatory facts: DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart for $17B, Marvell is in talks for Lumentum, GE Vernova bought $9B of grid, and Nvidia drew a DOJ antitrust probe over the Hugging Face deal plus a reported Chinese intelligence operation targeting Jensen Huang.
Housing deteriorated further: DR Horton's FY2027 guidance disappointed and the Bank of Canada hiked, warning of a subdued housing outlook — the rate relief the sector was underwriting is receding.

The regime probabilities shifted again toward the barbell: Stagflation 32.6 (+13.5) and Reflation 31.3 (+12.2) both rising, Goldilocks collapsing -13.2 to 17.7. Energy flows eased from 96 to 88 but remain dominant; Communication Services deteriorated further to -82.
